easy.def: Not exact; true for most things.
examples: The general rule is no running.
I have a general idea.
He gave a general answer.

more.def: Including or true for most people or things, and not exact.
examples: She gave us a general idea of how the game works.
The general rule is to put away your toys.
There was a general feeling of excitement.

easy.def: A very high leader in the army.
examples: The general led his soldiers.
The general gave an order.
A general sat at the table.

more.def: A very high officer in the army.
examples: The general planned the march across the mountains.
Soldiers saluted the general.
The general met with leaders from other countries.
It was generous of you to share your snack.
The generous girl gave me half her snack.
My aunt is generous with hugs.

more.def: Willing to give time, money, or help to others freely.
examples: Our generous neighbor gave vegetables from her garden to everyone on the street.
He was generous with his time and helped every student.
A generous gift helped the town build a new playground.

easy.def: A person who is very, very smart.
examples: He is a genius.
The genius solved the puzzle.
A genius made it.

more.def: A person who has an unusually high ability to think or create.
examples: The young girl was a math genius.
The scientist was a genius.
The musician was a genius who wrote songs at age five.
Be gentle with the baby.
The gentle horse let me pet it.
Use a gentle voice in the library.

more.def: Kind, calm, and careful; not rough or strong.
examples: A gentle rain fell on the garden all morning.
The nurse was gentle when she cleaned the cut.
A gentle breeze moved the leaves.

easy.def: A man who is polite and kind.
examples: The gentleman held the door for us.
Grandpa is a true gentleman.
Two gentlemen sat on a bench.

more.def: A man who is polite and well-behaved, or any man when you are speaking politely.
examples: The old gentleman tipped his hat to everyone he met.
Ladies and gentlemen, please take your seats because the show is starting.
A gentleman always lets others go first through the door.

easy.def: To have something come to you or to go and bring it.
examples: I get a new book today.
Please get your coat.
She got a letter.

more.def: To receive or obtain something, or to go and bring it back.
examples: My sister got a bike for her birthday.
Can you get the scissors from the kitchen drawer?
We get snow here almost every winter.
I get sleepy at night.
It gets cold in winter.
She got tall this year.

more.def: To change into a different condition or state.
examples: The sky gets dark when a storm is coming.
He got nervous before the spelling bee.
Ice cream gets soft if you leave it in the sun.
